# XVAL: AA-pattern fused stream-collide — acceptance against Ghia et al. (1982)

**Anchor**: `XVAL-LBM-AA-PATTERN-FUSED-STREAM-COLLIDE` (lanl/MF-LBM `aa-pattern-fused-stream-collide`)
**Acceptance (feature ledger)**: `< 15 %` against a reference; owner precision standard: >15 % is not acceptable.
**Generated by** `benchmarks/xval/aa_fused_cavity_doc.py` from `artifacts/xval_aa_pattern/cavity_verdict.json` (no hand-typed digits).

## 1. What was outstanding

`docs/xval_aa_pattern_fused_stream_collide_ordering.md` (m21666) fixed a BLOCKING operator-ordering defect (`C∘S` instead of the AA fused pull `S[C]`) and a mass-leaking wall treatment, and then withdrew every cavity number of the 2026-11-13 report. Its remaining-work item 1 was explicit:

> *Cavity ablation not finished. Until it lands, the anchor's `< 15 %` acceptance is not demonstrated for this module.*

`benchmarks/xval/aa_fused_cavity_acceptance.py` (m21739) built the harness that produces the number but only the L = 32 arm ran locally; L = 64/128/192 were left to scheduler shards.

## 2. Why the sweep stalled (root cause, not a guess)

One step is `9 x (L+2)^2` float64 **and ~60 torch kernel launches**, i.e. launch-overhead bound. On a 128-core host the default intra-op pool is 128 threads, and pool hand-off dominates the arithmetic. Measured in one process, `aa_fused_step`, L = 64:

| torch intra-op threads | ms / step |
|---|---|
| 128 (host default) | 26.1 |
| 16 | 6.5 |
| 8 | 6.2 |
| 4 | 5.9 |
| 2 | 5.9 |
| 1 | 7.0 |

4.4x of wall clock is spent handing work to idle threads. The driver now pins the pool (`TLBM_THREADS`, default 2) and `tests/test_aa_fused_cavity_verdict.py::test_acceptance_driver_pins_intraop_threads` keeps it pinned. Without the pin, an L = 64 arm (a few CPU-minutes of real work) sat `running` in the scheduler for > 6 h.

## 3. Setup

| item | value |
|---|---|
| solver | `tensorlbm.aa_fused_stream_collide.aa_fused_step` (AA fused pull + halfway bounce-back) |
| collision | D2Q9 BGK, float64 |
| cavity | lid-driven, Re = 100 (`U = 0.1`, `nu = U L / Re`, `tau = 0.5 + 3 nu`) |
| wall | halfway bounce-back, moving lid on the top solid row, 2000-step velocity ramp |
| reference | Ghia, Ghia & Shin (1982) Tables I/II, `benchmarks/anchors/ghia1982_provenance.json` (BOUND to OCR witness, sha256 recorded) |
| metric | `L2 = sqrt(mean((u_lattice/U - u_ghia)^2))` on the centre lines, normalised **before** subtracting |
| gate | `max(L2_u, L2_v) < 15 %`; informative second gate `< 3 %` |

The metric has a known half-cell floor (`metric_floor` per grid, column below) because the solver is cell-centred and the reference samples the walls: an *exact* profile fed back through the metric still scores the floor. Interior columns exclude the two extrapolated wall endpoints.

## 6. Notes / limitations

1. The cavity numbers certify the **fixed** kernel only. The 2026-11-13 `L2_u = 0.247` table was produced by the `C∘S` operator with a mass-leaking post-stream bounce-back and is superseded, not merely revised.
2. D2Q9/BGK, 2-D, `Re = 100` only. Nothing here transfers to MRT or D3Q19/27 without re-running the same gates.
3. `L2_v` is dominated by the metric floor on coarse grids (see the `metric floor u` column); the interior columns are the honest accuracy statement and the worst case over *both* components is what the gate uses.
4. Convergence monitoring uses `rtol = 1e-9` on the max velocity change per 1000 steps; arms that did not reach it are reported with `converged at = n/a` and their last-step residual, never as converged.
5. The interior `L2_u` falls to within ~2x of the metric floor (`floor_u_interior` in the artifact) already on the coarsest grid, so the fitted order is floor-limited and must not be read as the scheme's asymptotic order; the convergence figure plots both the error and the floor so the floor-limited region is visible. The `L2_v` series is nearly grid-independent (~4.5 % at L = 32/64/128), i.e. a *systematic* component dominates it (corner singularities of the moving lid and the half-cell extrapolation of the reference at the wall), not the discretisation of the bulk; it is reported as an open item, not explained away.
6. The ordering defect is O(2e-3) per step in smooth flows, which a `< 3 %` end-to-end gate can pass *despite*; structural equivalence (`torch.equal` against the canonical operator) remains the primary gate for the *pattern*, and this document is the accuracy gate for the *solution*.
